g.text: NEGOTIATION LEVERS · FINAL NEGOTIATING PRIORITY
Protect 8% first; request A, then B
Preserve or seek the 8% preferred return. Lead with A; if A is refused, pursue B.Use the standard hurdle as a fallback request only where it is absent.
Priority
Specific request
What makes it a concession?
Foundation: 8% protection
1 — Lead with A
2 — If A is refused, pursue B
Fallback request where absent
Confirm annual compounding, return of contributed capital including fees, and the existing catch-up clause. Preserve stronger existing protection.
8% preferred return, no GP catch-up, 20% carry.
Retain the 8% preferred return; full catch-up targeting 15%; 15% carry.
8% preferred return, full catch-up, 20% carry.
An existing hurdle is not a new concession.
First economic choice at the assigned 20% growth; +$17.92m if the reference hurdle already exists.
Acceptable alternative; +$16.59m on the same conditional comparison.
Adds protection only if not already provided; otherwise the status quo.
Do not surrender an existing preferred return to obtain 15% carry. Do not count the already-offered 1.35% fee as a new negotiating win.
Why this order: an effective preferred return has stronger contemporary market support; A creates $1.33m more inception NPV at 20% growth;the small gap makes an achievable B valuable.
If TPG refuses amendments: keep existing protection, accept the fee cut available to all LPs, seek better terms in future funds, and decidethe $75m question separately on the available terms.
Source: Case pp. 1, 4–6; Q5 Analysis!C10, D10, G10; Metrick & Yasuda (2007); Apollo S-1 (2008). No acceptance probabilities are modelled; above about 20.9% growth B leads A.
